# Sprout Social to cut 260 jobs as AI reshapes software industry

By [Shubhangi Chowdhury](https://americanbazaaronline.com/author/shubhangi/) July 15, 2026 2 Mins Read

[](https://americanbazaaronline.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/Layoff.jpg "Sprout Social to cut 260 jobs as AI reshapes software industry")

Share

[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Famericanbazaaronline.com%2F2026%2F07%2F15%2Fsprout-social-to-cut-260-jobs-as-ai-reshapes-software-industry-484641%2F "Facebook") [Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Famericanbazaaronline.com%2F2026%2F07%2F15%2Fsprout-social-to-cut-260-jobs-as-ai-reshapes-software-industry-484641%2F&text=Sprout%20Social%20to%20cut%20260%20jobs%20as%20AI%20reshapes%20software%20industry "Twitter") [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Famericanbazaaronline.

Sprout Social is laying off about 20% of its workforce, affecting roughly 260 employees, as the social media management company restructures its business amid rapid changes across the software industry.
The company began notifying affected employees on Wednesday. Chief Executive Ryan Barretto said the decision reflects broader shifts in how software companies are operating as artificial intelligence reshapes business priorities and investment strategies.

“Our industry, and software more broadly, is changing quickly,” he said. “The way companies need to operate and invest has changed with it.”

[**READ: Meta layoff forces H-1B worker to leave US**](https://americanbazaaronline.com/2026/07/14/meta-layoff-forces-h-1b-worker-to-leave-us-484582/) (July 14, 2026)

The [layoffs](https://www.marketwatch.com/story/sprout-social-to-cut-20-of-workforce-as-ai-fueled-tech-layoffs-continue-7e2b1b17?mod=markets) follow Sprout’s recent push into AI. In May, the company introduced an AI-powered social intelligence platform aimed at helping businesses better manage their social media presence.
It also expanded Trellis, its agentic AI engine, with new capabilities for publishing content and analyzing social media data.

Sprout joins a growing list of technology companies that have cited AI-driven changes while reducing headcount. Oracle said in June that it eliminated 21,000 jobs as it redirected spending toward AI initiatives. Cisco and Meta have also announced workforce reductions of 20% and 10%, respectively, while pointing to evolving business priorities.

Among the largest layoffs this year, Block, the parent company of Square and Cash App, said it would cut 40% of its workforce, stating that AI had fundamentally changed how the company operates.

[**READ: Wells Fargo layoffs renew debate over H-1B hiring**](https://americanbazaaronline.com/2026/06/22/wells-fargo-layoffs-renew-debate-over-h-1b-hiring-483268/) (June 22, 2026)
Sprout expects the restructuring to result in pre-tax charges of between $18 million and $20 million, largely related to severance and employee benefits. The company said most of those costs will be recorded during the third quarter, when the layoffs are expected to be completed.

Employees affected by the cuts will receive 12 weeks of base pay, plus an additional week of salary for each year of service. The company will also provide six months of fully paid healthcare coverage, a cash payment equal to the value of equity scheduled to vest over the next 90 days, and three months of outplacement assistance.

The announcement comes after Sprout reported stronger financial performance in its most recent quarter. In May, the company posted higher revenue and a narrower loss. On Wednesday, it also said it expects its results for the quarter ended in June to come in at the high end of its previously issued guidance.

# Sprout Social Announces Major Workforce Reduction and Expects Strong Q2 Results

## Key Points

* **Sprout Social, Inc. (NASDAQ: SPT)** expects Q2 2026 financial results at the high end of its previously issued guidance for revenue, non-GAAP operating income, and non-GAAP net income per share.
* The company is implementing a significant **workforce reduction of approximately 20%** , affecting around 260 employees.
* Estimated **pre-tax restructuring charges** related to the workforce reduction are in the range of **\\$18.0 million to \\$20.0 million** , with most charges recognized in Q3 2026.
* The restructuring is designed to align the company’s cost structure with its strategic focus on AI-powered social intelligence and to create a more resilient business model amid rapid industry changes.

## Detailed Analysis

On July 15, 2026, Sprout Social, Inc. announced two major developments that could significantly impact the company’s future outlook and potentially its share price:

### 1\. Preliminary Q2 2026 Results Exceeding Expectations

Sprout Social disclosed that it now expects its financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, to be at the **high end of its previously communicated outlook ranges** . This includes expectations for revenue, non-GAAP operating income, and non-GAAP net income per share.
These updated projections are based on preliminary, unaudited financial data and are subject to final accounting and review. The company will officially report Q2 results after market close on **Thursday, August 6, 2026** .

**Implication:** This signals robust business performance for Q2, which may provide positive momentum for the stock, especially as the company is outperforming its earlier guidance. However, investors should note that these are preliminary numbers and are subject to change.

### 2\. Major Workforce Reduction and Organizational Restructuring

In a major strategic move, Sprout Social’s Board of Directors approved a **workforce reduction plan** on July 8, 2026:

* Approximately **20% of the workforce** , or about 260 employees, to be laid off.
* The layoffs began on July 15, 2026.
* Estimated **pre-tax restructuring charges** between **\\$18 million and \\$20 million** , mainly for severance and employee benefits, to be recorded primarily in Q3 2026.
* The company expects to substantially complete the restructuring by the end of Q3 2026, subject to local law and consultation requirements.
* These charges will be excluded from non-GAAP financial measures.
* The plan is intended to streamline Sprout Social’s organizational structure and align its cost base with strategic priorities, particularly investments in AI-powered social intelligence.

In a letter to employees and stakeholders, CEO Ryan Barretto emphasized that the decision was not a reflection of the affected employees’ talent or commitment, but rather a strategic response to a rapidly changing software and social intelligence landscape. The company aims to build a more focused and durable business and act from a position of strength. Support for departing employees includes 12 weeks of pay, vesting of equity that would have vested in the next 90 days, and three months of outplacement support.

### Potential Impact and Shareholder Considerations
* **Price Sensitivity:** Both the positive Q2 outlook and the significant cost-reduction plan are potentially price-moving events. Investors may react positively to the improved profitability outlook, but large-scale layoffs and restructuring charges can also create uncertainty regarding future growth, morale, and execution risk.
* **Strategic Refocus:** The restructuring underscores a pivot toward AI-powered solutions, which could position Sprout Social competitively, but involves risks such as potential operational disruption and challenges in talent retention.
* **Forward-Looking Statements:** Management cautions that actual results and restructuring costs may differ materially from current estimates, and that the company may incur additional costs not currently anticipated.

## Exhibits and Supporting Information

* **Exhibit 99.1:** CEO Ryan Barretto’s letter to employees and stakeholders outlining the rationale and support measures for affected employees.

## Conclusion
Sprout Social’s announcement delivers a dual message of financial strength in the near term and decisive cost restructuring for the future. While the expected strong Q2 results are a positive indicator for shareholders, the large-scale workforce reduction and associated restructuring charges introduce short-term uncertainty. The company’s strategic pivot to AI-powered solutions may provide long-term benefits, but investors should closely monitor execution risks and future updates from management.

The company began notifying affected employees on July 15, 2026.
The plan is designed to restructure the company's organizational structure and align its cost base with its strategic priorities, including investments in AI-powered social intelligence.

Sprout Social estimates it will incur total pre-tax restructuring charges of approximately $18.0 million to $20.0 million, consisting primarily of cash expenditures related to employee severance payments and benefits. The company expects to recognize substantially all of these charges in the third quarter of 2026.

The company expects to substantially complete the plan by the end of the third quarter of 2026, subject to local law and consultation requirements.
